The same run independently reproduced the multiset-blindness half of this law at a second, unrelated site: probe Q rewrote `j = firstgetidx % 4; firstgetidx++;` as `j = firstgetidx++ % 4;`, which probe.py scored NEUTRAL-REARRANGED with real, count and multiset ALL flat, and which measured a fresh-fuzzy gain of 95.7964 -> 96.2649 with the modulo cluster order-aligned to target.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. Applies to a scalar self-update `x = x <op> K` whose old value is still read by statements the scheduler could move the update above, where the target stream shows the update writing back into the variable's own register. Says nothing about self-updates with no later reader of the old value, nothing about aggregate or memory-to-memory updates, and nothing about integer self-updates, none of which were tested. Companion to claim.law.IH_multiset-gain-does-not-imply-fuzzy-gain-arbitrate-with-count-distance and claim.law.PC_real-and-multiset-agreement-does-not-license-a-keep-without-fresh-fuzzy: this is the case where the multiset is not merely a weak arbiter but a structurally blind one.

falsifier: Produce an MWCC 1.2.5 function in which `x op= K;` and `x = (T)(x op K);` compile to byte-identical instruction streams at a site where the aligned view shows the assignment form allocating a FRESH destination register while a later reader of the old x still exists -- that would show the write-back target is not the lever. Or, conversely, find a site where the COMPOUND form is the one that allocates a fresh register and hoists: that would bound this law to the specific operator or type tested here rather than to the write-back target. The direct check on the recorded instance is `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/player do_players 0x47c:0x4c0 --diff`, which must read all rows `=` or `~`; restoring line 1802 to the assignment form must reintroduce the six-instruction ours-only block at +0x484 and drop fresh fuzzy back to 95.7964 from 96.3552.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: WRITING A SELF-UPDATE AS THE COMPOUND OPERATOR (`x *= K;`) RATHER THAN AS THE EQUIVALENT ASSIGNMENT (`x = (T)(x * K);`) MAKES MWCC REUSE x's OWN REGISTER FOR THE RESULT, AND REUSING THE REGISTER IS WHAT PREVENTS THE SCHEDULER FROM HOISTING THE COMPUTATION ABOVE THE STATEMENTS THAT STILL READ THE OLD VALUE. The two forms are semantically identical -- both promote to double, multiply, and round back with frsp -- and the assignment form is what a decompiler naturally emits, so this is a spelling difference that reads as cosmetic and is not. Measured on do_players at +0x484 (src/game/game/player.c line 1802, `len = (f32)(len * 0.667);` -> `len *= 0.667;`). WHAT THE ASSIGNMENT FORM COSTS: MWCC allocated a SECOND FPR for the result (`fmul f2,f26,f1`), which left the old value in f1 live alongside it, and having both live it was then free to hoist the whole `fmul` / `frsp` / `fcmpo` chain UP into the three preceding scaling triples that read the old value -- producing a six-instruction block at the wrong offset, with the multiply's operands in the opposite order from target (`fmul f2,f26,f1` against target's `fmul f1,f1,f26`). WHAT THE COMPOUND FORM BUYS: MWCC wrote the result back into f1, which kills the old value at that point, which forces the chain to sit AFTER the last reader -- and the aligned view then read BYTE-IDENTICAL to target for all seventeen rows of the window including register allocation and operand order. THE MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE THIS LAW EXISTS TO CARRY: the residual was multiset-NEUTRAL by construction (six opcodes on each side, same bag, different order) and the instruction COUNT never moved, so `real` was the only text arbiter that saw anything at all -- real 1167 -> 1153 -- while the opcode multiset sat flat at 15t before and after. Fresh objdiff fuzzy went 95.2683 -> 95.7964. A lane that screens order-only clusters on the multiset will conclude there is nothing there; the multiset is a BAG and is blind to placement by definition. Read `--ops` clusters whose two sides carry the same opcodes as SCHEDULE work with a source lever, not as noise. GENERALISATION AND ITS BOUNDARY: the lever is the WRITE-BACK TARGET, not the operator token, so it should apply to `+=`, `-=`, `|=` and `&=` wherever the target reuses the variable's register and ours allocates a fresh one; it says nothing about a self-update whose old value has NO later reader, where both forms are free to schedule identically, and nothing about integer self-updates (untested here). It is also NOT a licence to convert self-updates in bulk: do_players contains nine further `x = x <op> y` statements (lines 1758, 1769, 1806-1808, 1885, 1914, 1974, 2103) and none was converted, because the lever only pays where the aligned view actually shows a hoisted chain and a surplus destination register.
